language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I'm Rocío! We live here on an island, far into the Atlantic Ocean. It's beautiful here and we can live from farming and fishing.

You know, everything in our lives depends on water. We sail the ocean to catch fish, we need rain for our crops, we need water to drink, and so do all the animals on our farm. Did you know that our body consist of 60% of water? Water is everywhere!
Why don't you take a trip with me around the island, and I'll explain all about the "water cycle."
The amount of water on the planet is always the same, there is never more, and there is never less water. It just keeps moving in circles. The sun is the motor of all of this.
The sun heats the ocean, causing the water to get warmer and evaporate.
Now in gas form, the water rises up into the air and gets blown up into the sky. Here the water cools down and forms tiny drops. Millions of those drops together form a cloud.

When it starts raining, little drops fall from the sky. Some of the water goes back into the ocean, and some lands on the ground. On the land, the rain makes rivers that flow back to the ocean. That's how the water cycle works!

You might remember that water is quite a shape changer. Water can have three different forms: solid, liquid and gas.
And water can move between these states through the processes of evaporation, condensation, and freezing. Let's see what you still remember.
